subject: Physics
stem: By which of the following processes is the water heated?
solution: Water is usually heated by convection. Convection is a process of heat transfer that occurs when the particles of a medium move. Water is a poor conductor of heat. When heated, the water molecules at the bottom expand and become lighter. The heated water rises to the top. The cooler water from the sides moves down to the heat source. This process is repeated until all the water reaches the same temperature.

subject: Physics
stem: A man on a moving train throws a ball straight up in the air. Assuming the train is moving at a constant speed, where will the ball land?
solution: According to the principle of inertia, the ball inherits the horizontal velocity of the train. As the train is moving at a constant speed, the ball moves forward with same velocity as the train while it rises and falls. Hence, the ball lands back in his hand.

subject: Physics
stem: Specific heat of a substance depends upon which of the following?
solution: The specific heat of a substance is mainly determined by the material it is made of. Specific heat is the amount of heat required to raise the temperature of one gram of a substance by one degree Celsius. It is expressed in units of joules per gram per degree Celsius (J/g°C).

subject: Physics
stem: Which of the following will form a virtual and erect image for all positions of the object?
solution: A convex mirror will form a virtual and erect image for all positions of the object. Convex mirrors are diverging in nature and produce virtual and erect images for all positions of the object. The image formed by a convex mirror is always virtually erect and diminished. Convex mirrors are used as rear-view mirrors to capture a wider field of view. A concave mirror will produce virtual as well as real images, depending upon the position of the object.

subject: Physics
stem: For which of the following is the refractive index of a material greatest?
solution: The refractive index of a material is greatest for violet light. The refractive index of a material is a measure of how much light bends as it passes through the material. It’s calculated by dividing the speed of light in air by the speed of light in the material. The refractive index is inversely proportional to the wavelength of light, so violet light has the highest refractive index because it has the shortest wavelength.

subject: Physics
stem: Light can be polarised which of the following?
solution: Light can be polarised by all of the following processes: reflection, refraction and scattering. Other processes that can produce polarised light include absorption, diffraction and birefringence. Polarisation by scattering occurs when scattered light is viewed in a direction perpendicular to the direction of incidence. The light is then found to be plane polarised.

subject: Physics
stem: A galvanometer can be converted into an ammeter by connecting:
solution: We can convert a galvanometer into an ammeter by connecting a low resistance in parallel. Electric current is defined as the rate of flow of charge or electron, so its direction is the flow of positive charge. Resistance is the opposition delivered by the conductor through which current flows. A device that is used to measure electric current in a circuit is called an ammeter. The resistance of an ideal ammeter is always zero and is always connected in series within the circuit. A galvanometer is a device that is used to detect and measure small electric currents in any circuit. It can measure current up to 10–6 amperes.

subject: Physics
stem: In a step up transformer, the value of the current in the secondary coil, in comparison to primary coil is
solution: In a step-up transformer, the current in the secondary coil is less than the current in the primary coil. A step-up transformer increases the voltage while decreasing the current. The secondary voltage is higher than the primary voltage. To keep the primary and secondary power of the system equal, the step- up transformer decreases the secondary current compared to the primary current.

subject: Physics
stem: The atom bomb is based on the principle of:
solution: An atomic bomb is based on the principle of nuclear fission. Nuclear fission is a nuclear reaction where the nucleus of an atom splits into two or more smaller nuclei. This process releases a large amount of energy and often produces gamma photons.

solution: The rise of a liquid in a capillary tube is due to surface tension. This phenomenon is also known as capillary action.

solution: The unit of surface tension is dyne cm–1 in the Centimeter Gram Second (CGS) system of units. Surface tension is the force per unit length caused by the attraction of the particles in a liquid’s surface layer to the bulk of the liquid.

solution: Water boils at a lower temperature on high altitudes because atmospheric pressure is low.

subject: Chemistry
stem: How many elements are present in the third period of the periodic table?
solution: The third period contains eight elements because it corresponds to the filling of the 3s and 3p subshells (of the third shell), which take a total of 8 electrons, two in the 3s and 6 in the 3p subshell.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which of the following holds true for the elements of the same group in the periodic table?
solution: Elements in the same group of the periodic table have the same number of valence electrons. They also have similar chemical properties. Valence is a measure of an atom’s ability to combine with other atoms to form chemical compounds or molecules.

subject: Chemistry
stem: What is the atomicity of inert gases?
solution: The number of atoms present in a single molecule is termed as its atomicity. All inert gases are monoatomic, meaning their molecules contain only one atom. Therefore, the atomicity of inert gases is 1.

subject: Chemistry
stem: According to the modern periodic law, the physical and chemical properties of elements are periodic functions of which of the following?
solution: According to the modern periodic law, the physical and chemical properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic number and electronic configuration. The modern periodic law states that when elements are arranged in order of increasing atomic numbers, their properties repeat after regular intervals. This is because an atom’s electronic configuration is directly related to its atomic number.

subject: Chemistry

stem: The correct order of reactivity of the following metals is
solution: The correct order of reactivity for the metals sodium (Na), magnesium (Mg), zinc (Zn), and iron (Fe) is Na > Mg > Zn > Fe. The reactivity series, also known as the activity series, arranges metals in order of decreasing reactivity. The reactivity series can be used to determine if a metal can displace another in a single displacement reaction.

stem: Which of the following are present inside the atoms?
solution: Atoms are made up of protons, electrons, and neutrons, which are subatomic particles. Protons: Positively charged particles found in the nucleus of an atom. Neutrons: Uncharged particles found in the nucleus of an atom. Electrons: Negatively charged particles found outside the nucleus of an atom. The number of protons in an atom’s nucleus defines the element.

subject: Chemistry
stem: According to Dalton’s atomic theory, an atom:
solution: According to John Dalton’s atomic theory, an atom cannot be subdivided. Atoms are indivisible. Dalton’s atomic theory states that atoms are the smallest particles of matter and cannot be divided into smaller particles.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Atomic Number, Mass Number and Subatomic Particles
stem: The atomic weight of an atom is due to which of the following?
solution: The atomic weight of an atom is the total weight of the atom, which is approximately equal to the number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus. The mass of electrons is negligible, therefore they contribute little to the atomic weight.

subject: Chemistry

solution: Brass is a mixture (alloy) of copper and zinc, and the ratio of the two metals varies between different samples. Marble is a compound CaCO3. Washing soda is a compound with the chemical formula Na2CO3. Quick lime is a compound with the chemical formula CaO.

subject: Physics
stem: Which of the following is not a derived unit?
solution: The hertz (symbol: Hz) is the derived unit of frequency in the International System of Units (Sl) and is defined as one cycle per second. It is named for Heinrich Rudolf Hertz. Plank’s constant: Planck’s Constant relates the energy of light photons to their frequency. Its value is 6.626 × 10–34 Js. Gravitational acceleration: The acceleration produced in the motion of a body under the effect of gravity is called acceleration due to gravity. It is denoted by g = G R m 2 The acceleration due to gravity on the surface of the Earth is given by, where G = universal gravitational constant, M = mass of the Earth and R = radius of the Earth. Electric current: It is a physical quantity for measuring electric current. Its unit is ampere. Therefore, electric current is not a derived quantity.

solution: The average velocity depends on the net displacement of a body. If a body starts from a position and returns to the same position after some time the net displacement is zero. Consequently, the average velocity is zero.

solution: A newborn infant has 300 bones in the body, out of which most of them fuse together becoming 206 bones in an adult.

solution: A species is the smallest unit of classification in biology because it is the basic unit for categorising organisms based on their structure, development and evolutionary history. A species is a group of organisms that are morphologically related and can interbreed. Family, class and genus are higher-order categories in taxonomic classification. Taxonomy is the branch of biology that deals with the identification and naming of organisms.

subject: Biology
stem: The deficiency of vitamin A causes which of the following?
solution: Vitamin A is an essential micronutrient that helps with vision, immune system strength and skin health. A deficiency in vitamin A can cause night blindness because the body stops producing pigments needed for the retina to function properly. In more severe cases, vitamin A deficiency can lead to blindness by damaging the retina and cornea. Vitamin D deficiency causes rickets. Vitamin E deficiency causes scurvy. Vitamin K deficiency leads to an increase in the clotting time.

solution: The kidneys responsible for water balance. They filter blood, remove waste and regulate fluid and electrolyte balance. When the body is dehydrated, the kidneys conserve water. When the body has excess water, the kidneys make urine more dilute to expel it. The kidneys are bean-shaped organs located in the back of the abdomen. Each kidney is made up of many microscopic tubules called nephrons.

subject: Biology

solution: Chlorophyll-containing autotrophic thallophytes are called algae. Algae are simple, thalloid, autotrophic organisms that contain chlorophyll and are mostly aquatic. They can be found in a variety of habitats, including moist stones, soils and wood. Algae are capable of making their own food through photosynthesis, which is made possible by the presence of green-coloured chlorophyll pigment.

subject: Biology
stem: Which of the following regulates the secretion of hormones from the pituitary gland?
solution: The hypothalamus is the gland that regulates the secretion of hormones from the pituitary gland. The hypothalamus receives signals from the brain, such as light exposure, temperature and feelings, and sends them to the pituitary gland. It also produces hormones that help regulate the pituitary gland, including corticotrophin-releasing hormone, dopamine, gonadotrophin releasing hormone, growth hormone releasing hormone, oxytocin, somatostatin and thyrotropin-releasing hormone. The pituitary gland is often called the “master gland” because of its role in controlling many other endocrine glands.

stem: Melting of ice at its melting point is which of the following processes?
solution: The melting of ice at its melting point is an isothermal process. During melting, the energy goes towards changing the phase of the substance, not its temperature. Isochoric process: Volume of the system remains constant in an isochoric process. Adiabatic process: Heat content of the system remains constant in an adiabatic process.

solution: The atomic masses of elements are usually fractional because they are a mixture of isotopes of different masses. The atomic mass of an element is the average of the atomic masses of all its isotopes, weighted by their natural abundances. The atomic masses listed in the periodic table are the average atomic masses of the elements.
